newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France head warns pilots on strike.
newsitem.headline: Air France head warns pilots on strike.

text.p: The chairman of airline Air France gave a formal warning to pilots who have called a four-day strike starting next Sunday and said the stoppage would cost more than one billion francs ($180 million).
Christian Blanc issued the warning at a board meeting on Wednesday.

The SNPL pilots union then stepped up the pressure, issuing a statement which said Blanc had announced he would resign if a planned strike was not called off but a company spokeswoman denied he made such a remark.

"No it's not true. Christian Blanc did not say he would resign. He simply said he would draw all the consequences of the strike at the next board meeting on March 27," an Air France spokeswoman told Reuters.
Air France pilots have called for a strike on March 23 to 26 inclusive and another stoppage for the end of April.
The strike was "indefensible (and) will have a cataclysmic economic and commercial effect on the company and will cost more than one billion francs," the statement said.
The strike was called to oppose the planned recruitment of 450 younger pilots, who would join on a lower pay scale, at a time when 800 more experienced pilots are unemployed.
The company reiterated that it would break even this year. It added that its development required the company to adjust to standards of the market in terms of costs and revenues.
Its pilots' pay was higher than that of its European and U.S. rivals, particularly for new hires at the beginning of their careers.
